claim_in_erdem: the whole group of ff. 182(183)a-199b and 228b-235a is al-Khwarizmi's (Erdem p. 164)
item_level_evidence: the article itself states that his name appears only on chapters 39 and 52 (p. 164); one tract (chapter 38) is ascribed in the witness to Umayr ibn Saman (Charette and Schmidl p. 108)
result: not supported: two ascriptions to al-Khwarizmi and one to another person within the group

claim_in_erdem: King established the attribution of the group (Erdem p. 164)
item_level_evidence: King (1983a: 2), as quoted by Charette and Schmidl (p. 107), states that the attribution of each text is an open problem

claim_in_erdem: a complete sine of 150, borrowed from Brahmagupta, marks al-Khwarizmi's time (Erdem p. 164)
item_level_evidence: the same base is used in Texts 1, 8 and 10 of B; Charette and Schmidl treat it as a sign of the early ninth century (p. 163), not of one author; chapter 1 uses a radius of 60 (Erdem p. 173)

claim_in_erdem: the group is one work divided into 59 chapters (Erdem p. 165)
item_level_evidence: the group lies in two blocks separated by the works of ff. 200v-227v (PAL; Erdem p. 164); the list skips chapter 57; chapter 41 lacks its beginning; the folios of chapters 2-3 are given as 228b and as 182b; PAL catalogues 228v-231r as anonymous and 231v-235r as al-Khwarizmi's
result: not supported; Charette and Schmidl call it an illusory unity (p. 107)

item_level_evidence: the table of chapter 30 (Text 11) rests on the obliquity 23;33, first observed in 213 H (828-29), so it is later than c. 830 (Charette and Schmidl p. 183); Erdem himself suggests that the chapters with plane trigonometry are earlier than those with spherical trigonometry (Turkish version p. 205)
result: the group is not of one date

claim_in_erdem: the qibla chapters 20-25 are al-Khwarizmi's (Erdem pp. 165-171)
item_level_evidence: a textual coincidence with the anonymous Tashkent manuscript (King) and a similar 20 x 20 table ascribed to al-Khwarizmi in Cairo, Taymur 103/2 (p. 171)
result: a parallel, not an ascription in the witness; the strongest case in the group after chapters 39 and 52
